minutes.headline: Board recommends town meeting approve ADU zoning change that drops the owner-occupancy requirement
minutes.summary: The Planning Board approved a de minimis site-plan change for 110 Pleasant Street, then closed a public hearing (no members of the public attended) and voted to recommend town meeting approval of two warrant articles: a state-mandated ADU zoning update and a flood insurance rate map/floodplain bylaw update. The bulk of the meeting was spent debating whether to create a new standard operating procedure letting applicants pre-pay a 53G peer-review fee, ending with a vote to simply enforce the $2,000 peer-review deposit already written into the rules and regulations rather than adopt a new procedure.

Close the public hearing for the ADU and flood insurance rate map update bylaws.
Recommend approval of the ADU zoning bylaw to annual town meeting.
Recommend approval of the floodplain bylaw update to annual town meeting.
Enforce the standard operating procedures (53G peer review fee) as already written in the rules and regulations, rather than adopt a new SOP.
Approve the Planning Board's minutes from the April 14th, 2025 meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair proposed making it an explicit option for applicants to pre-pay a peer-review deposit, commonly around this figure, before the board formally requests review.

budget_items.topic: 53G project review fee, existing rules and regs
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member read the existing rules and regulations showing this deposit is already due at time of application with the balance due afterward, arguing the requirement already exists and should simply be enforced.

decisions.decision: Rather than individually notifying residents affected by the flood map change (deemed not feasible with current staffing), the office will print handout instructions for using the federal online tool so residents can check their own property at town meeting.
The chair will raise the floodplain/FEMA mapping issue at the following night's Select Board meeting so the public is aware.
The chair will present the ADU and floodplain articles at town meeting as previously done, with a board member free to raise the owner-occupancy point from the floor if desired.
The MBTA Communities contractor is confirmed to present at the May 12th meeting as the first agenda item.
The board will aim to hold public information sessions on MBTA Communities options before the June 23rd meeting, since there is no second May meeting.
The board will use an informal 'patch' for the peer-review process now and hold off on any formal rules-and-regulations changes until the planner position is filled.
Going forward, items already required by the rules and regs but not clearly written into procedure will be documented in the SOP first, then folded into the rules and regs at a future public hearing.
Updating standard submission-requirement sheets for applicants will likely wait until fall given summer slowdown in town government.

what_happened.line: Board voted to recommend town meeting approve the state-mandated ADU zoning bylaw, which drops the owner-occupancy requirement.
Board voted to recommend town meeting approve an update to the floodplain and flood insurance rate map bylaw.
The public hearing on both bylaws closed with no residents attending or commenting.
Board voted to enforce the peer-review deposit already written into its rules and regulations rather than adopt a new fee procedure.
Board approved a de minimis site-plan change at 110 Pleasant Street for a foundation extension.

why_it_matters: Town meeting will be asked to vote on the ADU bylaw, which changes what accessory dwelling units can be built without an owner living on site.

The floodplain bylaw update ties to FEMA flood maps; residents in affected areas will get handout instructions at town meeting to check their own property against the federal tool rather than individual notice.
The peer-review fee decision keeps an existing an amount as heard deposit requirement in place for applicants going through board review, rather than creating a new pre-payment procedure.
